# sqlite-graph-memory

> Persistent memory for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any MCP client, built over a folder of markdown notes you already keep (Obsidian vaults included). Vector search finds entry points, the [[wikilinks]] in the notes are the graph, a cross-encoder reranks. One SQLite file for telemetry and the per-turn ledger, no graph database, no extraction pass. MIT, Python >= 3.9, version 0.3.1 on PyPI. Status: pilot.

Who it is for: one person or one agent setup with a markdown knowledge base that wants associative recall without running a graph database. Not a framework, not multi-tenant.

## Three commands

```bash
pip install 'sqlite-graph-memory[embeddings]'
sgm-index ./notes
sgm-ask --ab "In which programming language is the tool behind Project Ouzel written?"
```

`--ab` runs vector-only and vector+graph side by side and logs the difference to SQLite (`ab_recall` table). Other modes: `sgm-ask "q"` (vector only), `sgm-ask --graph "q"`, `sgm-ask --ask "q"` (context bundle to paste into an agent). The base install without `[embeddings]` explains the missing extra instead of failing with a traceback.

## MCP server

Command: `sgm-mcp` (also installed as `sqlite-graph-memory`, so `uvx --with 'sqlite-graph-memory[embeddings]' sqlite-graph-memory` works). Registry name: `io.github.tonydzi/sqlite-graph-memory`. One tool: `memory_recall`.

JSON clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed, Windsurf):

```json
{"mcpServers": {"sqlite-graph-memory": {"command": "sgm-mcp",
  "env": {"BRAIN_INDEX_DIR": "/path/to/your/index", "TURNSTATE_DB": "/path/to/your/turnstate.db"}}}}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add sqlite-graph-memory -e BRAIN_INDEX_DIR=/path/to/index -- sgm-mcp`

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.sqlite-graph-memory]
command = "sgm-mcp"
env = { BRAIN_INDEX_DIR = "/path/to/your/index" }
```

## Benchmark (memory-bench v0.1, bench/)

Synthetic 202-note vault, 91 questions (69 answerable, 22 with no answer in the vault). Every number is recomputed by CI from per-question outputs.

- sqlite-graph-memory, vector only (0.3.0): R@5 0.88, R@10 0.92
- sqlite-graph-memory, vector+graph (0.3.0): R@5 0.85, R@10 0.91
- bm25 reference: R@5 0.77, R@10 0.79

On this vault vector-only ranks ahead of graph mode overall. Run it: `python bench/run.py --system bm25` (stdlib only).

## Eval on your own notes (eval/)

The wikilinks you wrote are the relevance labels: no labelling budget, no LLM calls. Four question classes: title, body, bridge, temporal. Each scored in vector-only and vector+graph mode.

```bash
python eval/run_eval.py --selftest
python eval/build_gold.py /path/to/notes --n-per-class 60
python eval/run_eval.py --gold eval/gold-<date>.jsonl --sqlite
```

## Configuration (env only)

BRAIN_INDEX_DIR (index folder, default ./index), TURNSTATE_DB (default ./turnstate.db), BRAIN_ANSWER_OUT, BRAIN_AB_JSON (structured A/B output), AB_SOURCE, SGM_NO_STAR_PROMPT=1 (silence the one-time star line after --ab), SGM_CONFIG_DIR, SGM_PPR=1 (PageRank lane in the ordering, off by default). Full list: .env.example.
